transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Crescent Health), Jordan Lee (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (Security), Aisha Khan (Product), Tom - Director Ops

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna get into the POC success criteria sign-off. Elena and I will run through the acceptance tests, benchmarks and timelines. Maya, Jordan, Priya - thanks for being here.
[00:32] Maya: Yeah thanks Samir, appreciate it. We got your initial doc, a couple of comments in the sheet, but overall we want to lock down the go/no-go metrics.
[01:10] Elena: Cool, so quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan (hosted + dedicated), reporting format, and timelines. Then action items.
[01:45] Jordan: One thing up front - our main constraints are P95 latency under 400ms for interactive routes, sustain 200 rps for batch inference during peak windows, and cost needs to come in under our spend threshold.
[02:10] Priya: Security note - during POC we prefer hosted with strict data retention and KMS integration; if we see data residency gaps we'll push to private. We need SOC2 docs and assurance around audit logs.
[02:55] Samir: Understood. On the latency - our baseline suggestion is P95 < 350ms for the small prompt route and P95 < 600ms for long-form summarization. But since you asked 400ms, we can aim for <400ms for interactive default.
[03:30] Maya: That sounds reasonable. For acceptance tests on quality we want a go/no-go based on Rouge-L and some human evals. If automated metrics drop more than 3% relative to current production, it's a fail.
[04:05] Elena: Right, we'll include automated metrics (BLEU/Rouge-like proxy), plus a human eval sample of 200 prompts for qualitative scoring. Acceptance rule: mean human score >= 4.0/5 and no more than 10% critical failures.
[04:40] Tom: Quick clarification - what counts as a critical failure?
[04:50] Aisha: From product side, critical is PHI leakage, hallucination that alters clinical instruction, or incorrect patient-identifying statements.
[05:20] Priya: We need explicit redaction guidance and verification steps in the acceptance tests.
[05:40] Samir: We'll add a PHI leakage test to the acceptance suite - automated PII detectors plus manual review for flagged outputs.
[06:10] Jordan: About workload sizing - we'll share our traffic histogram, but peak concurrency looks like 200 active requests with a long tail to 600 over the hour. Average tokens per request ~120.
[06:40] Elena: That helps; for the benchmark we'll simulate the 95th percentile session mix, including the long-form summarization route at higher token counts. We'll produce per-route QPS and latency curves.
[07:05] Maya: We care about token-level cost too, can you include cost projection?
[07:15] Samir: Yes, report will include token cost, estimated monthly run-rate under your traffic profile, and delta vs your current infra.
[07:40] Elena: Benchmark plan: 1) run hosted config with perf profile, 2) run dedicated reserved capacity profile (lower variance), 3) run a cached scenario with KV prefix caching. We'll collect P50/P90/P95, throughput, token cost, and tail latency spikes.
[08:10] Jordan: How long will each run take?
[08:20] Elena: Each scenario is ~2 hours to warm up and capture steady-state results; we'll run multiple passes - plan ~6 hours total per environment. We'll provide scripts so you can reproduce locally if needed.
[08:50] Tom: If we need to test private deployment, what's the timeline?
[09:00] Samir: Private deployment takes longer - assuming standard network access and credentials, an on-prem or VPC setup for the POC is ~2-3 weeks. Hosted POC is much faster, we can start benchmarks within one week once we have sample traffic.
[09:30] Priya: For our security team, hosted is acceptable for the initial benchmark as long as you support customer-managed KMS and can sign a temporary DPA with agreed retention. We'll review your SOC2 report though.
[10:00] Elena: We'll attach SOC2 and our KMS integration doc. Also a checklist showing where audit logs flow.
[10:25] Maya: On acceptance tests - do you have a template for pass/fail scoring?
[10:35] Elena: Yes, we've got the POC acceptance spreadsheet. High-level: each route has functional tests (accuracy thresholds), perf tests (P95 target, throughput), security tests (no high-severity leaks), and operational tests (reliability during a simulated traffic spike). Each test yields Pass/Fail/Needs Review and contributes to an overall go/no-go.
[11:05] Samir: For go/no-go, we suggest: all critical security tests must pass; at least 90% of routes must meet perf thresholds; quality metrics cannot degrade >3% from baseline. If any of these are violated it's a no-go.
[11:40] Maya: That aligns with our internal risk appetite. Can we define the reporting format?
[11:50] Elena: We'll deliver a single PDF report plus a CSV with per-route time-series. Report sections: Executive summary, per-route metrics (P50/P90/P95, cost/token), acceptance test outcomes, and recommendations. We'll also include raw logs and reproduction scripts in a shared folder.
[12:20] Jordan: For the CSV, include columns: timestamp, route, qps, p50, p90, p95, avg_tokens, cost_tokens.
[12:45] Samir: Yep we'll mirror that. Also we'll include a short conformance table with boolean pass/fail per acceptance criterion.
[13:05] Aisha: Who signs off on the POC?
[13:10] Maya: Product and Data Science will sign off on quality; Security signs off on compliance items; Ops (Tom/Jordan) sign off on performance and cost.
[13:30] Priya: We'll expect an evidence bundle for security - log samples, KMS usage, and a statement about data retention.
[13:50] Samir: We'll provide those.
[14:05] Elena: About the human eval - we need to agree on label schema. We propose 1-5 for relevance, 1-5 for factuality, and binary flag for PHI leakage. We'll share the labeling instructions.
[14:35] Maya: OK, 200 samples is workable. We'll also seed it with 50 high-risk prompts.
[14:55] Jordan: On benchmarking harness - do you support running the harness against both hosted and a dedicated stack?
[15:05] Elena: Yes, our harness is environment-agnostic; you'll need an API key for hosted, and for dedicated we'll provide endpoints and region details plus an SSH key if running inside your VPC.
[15:30] Tom: Any special telemetry we should capture?
[15:40] Elena: Capture system metrics (GPU utilization, memory), and model-level metrics (KV cache hit rate, tokens/sec). For hosted tests we will provide GPU-aggregated metrics where possible.
[16:05] Priya: About KV cache - can you explain cache privacy? We don't want cached PHI accessible across customers.
[16:20] Elena: Caches are per-tenant; VPC/private setups have dedicated pools and no cross-tenant caching. On hosted, logical isolation and TTLs are enforced. We'll document TTL and eviction policy.
[16:50] Maya: How will you handle rollout if we hit quality regressions?
[16:55] Samir: We'll recommend fallback policies, e.g., route to a stable model variant or increase quantization fallback. For POC we can simulate fallbacks and ensure no user-visible errors.
[17:20] Aisha: Timeline recap?
[17:25] Samir: Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and share artifacts. Week 1: customer provides traffic + Redwood prepares harness. Week 2: benchmarks run. Week 3: human evals + security review. Week 4: consolidated report and decision meeting. So roughly 4 weeks for POC.
[18:00] Jordan: That schedule works for engineering.
[18:10] Maya: A couple of small ask - include token-cost sensitivity analysis and 95th percentile cost spikes in the report.
[18:25] Elena: We'll add cost sensitivity and a small model-swap comparison (e.g., 1.2x cheaper quantized variant).
[18:45] Samir: Ok, next steps and owners: I'll upload the acceptance spreadsheet, Elena will finalize harness and instructions, Jordan will share traffic, Priya will send compliance list.
[19:05] Maya: We'll aim to have the artifacts to you by Friday.
[19:20] Tom: And we'll schedule the benchmark run for week of Mar 10.
[19:35] Samir: Great. Any other questions?
[19:40] Priya: One more - how does Redwood store logs for hosted POC? Retention and redaction?
[19:50] Samir: By default logs retained 30 days; we can adjust retention and enable PII redaction on request. We'll document exact fields logged.
[20:05] Elena: Also note there may be intermittent transcription artifacts in our notes - sorry, old habit.
[20:15] Maya: Ha, fair.
[20:30] Samir: Alright, we'll share the artifacts by 2025-03-06. Thanks everyone.
[20:45] (call ends)

Notes:
- References shared: POC acceptance spreadsheet (link: https://drive.google.com/sheet/placeholder), Redwood POC template (https://redwood.ai/poc-template), SOC2 summary (attached).
- Acceptance criteria highlights: security must pass; perf thresholds P95 <400ms interactive, sustain 200 rps; quality degrade <3% relative to baseline; human eval >=4.0/5; <10% critical failures.
- Reporting format: PDF executive report + CSV time series + raw logs + reproduction scripts.

End of transcript.
